To fix Marginal Significance

What we found

You described 1 effect with terms related to ‘marginally significant’.

Show details

You described effects with terms related to ‘marginally significant’. If p values above 0.05 are interpreted as an effect, you inflate the alpha level, and increase the Type 1 error rate. If a p value is higher than the prespecified alpha level, it should be interpreted as a non-significant result.

To fix Exact P-Values

What we found

We found 10 imprecise p values out of 76 detected p values.

Show details

Reporting p values imprecisely (e.g., p < .05) reduces transparency, reproducibility, and re-use (e.g., in p value meta-analyses). Best practice is to report exact p-values with three decimal places (e.g., p = .032) unless p values are smaller than 0.001, in which case you can use p < .001.

This module sometimes flags false positives when sentences discuss how p-value thresholds were set. It can also miss an imprecise p-value that is reported against a threshold (e.g., “decreased at the p < .05 significance threshold”).

  • We assessed 12 R code files for reproducibility and ran them (each in an isolated Docker container).

To check (5)

To check Non-Significant P Value Check

What we found

We found 43 non-significant p values that should be checked for appropriate interpretation.

Show details

Meta-scientific research has shown nonsignificant p values are commonly misinterpreted. It is incorrect to infer that there is ‘no effect’, ‘no difference’, or that groups are ‘the same’ after p > 0.05.

It is possible that there is a true non-zero effect, but that the study did not detect it. Make sure your inference acknowledges that it is possible that there is a non-zero effect. It is correct to include the effect is ‘not significantly’ different, although this just restates that p > 0.05.

Metacheck does not yet analyze automatically whether sentences which include non-significant p-values are correct, but we recommend manually checking the sentences below for possible misinterpreted non-significant p values.

Working Directory (setwd)

Best programming practice is to avoid setwd() in analysis code: it hardcodes an assumption about the working directory (often an absolute path on the author’s own machine), so the code breaks when run anywhere else. Keep the working directory as the caller sets it and use relative paths. No setwd() calls were found in any of the code files.

Package Installation (install.packages)

Best programming practice is to avoid install.packages() in analysis code: it installs software on whoever runs the script without asking, which is at minimum disruptive (an unexpected install, network access, a package version the author never tested against) and at worst a security risk if it points at an untrusted repository. Document required packages instead (a README, or a list of them: an renv.lock/DESCRIPTION for R, a requirements.txt for Python). install.packages() calls were found in 2 code files.

Spreadsheet Formatting

We examined 7 spreadsheet files in the repository; 3 have at least one formatting issue.

File Sheet Issue Detail
Merged_raw_data_Unhealthy.xlsx Sheet 1 Empty or unnamed columns 2 columns are empty or have a blank header.
Merged_raw_data_Healthy.xlsx Sheet 1 Empty or unnamed columns 2 columns are empty or have a blank header.
Merged_raw_data_Control.xlsx Sheet 1 Empty or unnamed columns 2 columns are empty or have a blank header.

Spreadsheet formatting such as colour, merged cells, and blank rows/columns is not preserved when data are read programmatically or exported to CSV. Store data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable, no colour-encoded meaning) so it is machine-readable.

Careless Responding

1 distinct respondent was flagged for straightlining: giving the same answer for at least 80% of the items in a multi-item scale of 5 items or more. One respondent can be flagged in several scales; the table below is one row per person, and the Longest run column gives the run that triggered the strongest flag, so you can check it against the raw data.

These are prompts to inspect those rows, not definitive judgements.

Respondent Blocks flagged Scales Longest run Short-scale only
104354 1 q56 (0-10, 10 items) same answer 8 times in a row, out of 10 items (flagged at 8) no

What this does not cover. Only 1 of 8 data files could be screened: the rest had no detectable multi-item scale block, or too few respondents. Even in a screened file, these checks only look at multi-item rating scales — the only place where a repeated or flat answer pattern is interpretable. Single questions, open text, demographics and any item outside a detected scale block are never examined. A respondent can therefore answer most of a survey carelessly and still not be flagged here, and finding nothing is not evidence that a dataset is free of careless responding.

How to make your code run on another computer

We ran your code on a clean computer, the way a reader or reviewer would. Below is each problem we found, the scripts it affects, and how to fix it. Fix them in the order given: a problem near the top can cause the ones below it.

A script uses a location that exists only on your computer.

  • Preprocessing_EMA_IG.R reads C:/Users/leonardo.pimpini/Desktop/PROJECTS/ONGOING/EMA_Social_Media/ANALYSES/DATA_PREPROCESSING/Data/Merged_raw_data_Unhealthy.xlsx.

No other computer has that folder, and the file is also not in the deposit.

  1. Add the file to the deposit.
  2. In the script, write the location from the top folder of your project, such as data/survey.csv. In R, here::here(“data”, “survey.csv”) does this for you.
  3. Remove any setwd() lines.

A script could not open a file, but the error does not say which.

  • Extract_IG_use_minutes.R

Check every file the script reads. Make sure each one is in the deposit, and that its location is written from the top folder of the project.

A script runs longer than our limit of 5 minutes.

  • Intention_to_Snack_3way.R
  • intention_behavior_brms.R

State in the README how long each script runs. If some steps take hours, save their results (such as fitted models) to files, add those to the deposit, and let the script read them, so readers can check the rest without waiting.

Metacheck can’t automatically establish what caused the error, or how it should be improved.

  • Figure_GLMM_5_panels.R
  • Merge_Raw_data_EMA_IG_study.R

Comparison with the paper

Of the 95 statistical tests reported in the paper, 24 were found in the output of the code.

All details of the Reproducibility Check

This module assesses whether the paper’s code could be run on its data, and — because execute = TRUE — actually ran it. We examined 12 R code files.

Execution

The code was run. Each script ran in an isolated Docker container against a throwaway copy of the repository, in the run order above, with a 300-second per-script timeout. Of 12 scripts: 6 ran without error, 4 errored, 2 timed out, 0 could not run because one of its own dependencies is unavailable, 0 did not parse. Running against current package versions: a break can reflect version drift, which argues for pinning versions.

> X <- model.matrix(delete.response(terms(m_use)), pred_df)
> V <- vcov(m_use)

> pred_df$emmean <- as.numeric(X %*% beta)
> pred_se <- sqrt(diag(X %*% V %*% t(X)))
> pred_df$lower.CL <- pred_df$emmean - 1.96 * pred_se
> pred_df$upper.CL <- pred_df$emmean + 1.96 * pred_se

> day_grid <- 1:10
> pred_df <- expand.grid(
>   Day_nr = day_grid,
>   Group  = levels(dat$Group)
> )
> pred_df <- pred_df %>%
>   mutate(
>     Study_Phase = ifelse(Day_nr <= 5, "Pre-manipulation", "Manipulation"),
>     Study_Phase = factor(Study_Phase, levels = levels(dat$Study_Phase)),
>     Time_Phase = ifelse(Day_nr <= 5, Day_nr - 3, Day_nr - 8),
>     Group = factor(Group, levels = levels(dat$Group))
>   )
> X <- model.matrix(delete.response(terms(m_use)), pred_df)
> V <- vcov(m_use)
> beta <- fixef(m_use)
> pred_df$emmean <- as.numeric(X %*% beta)
> pred_se <- sqrt(diag(X %*% V %*% t(X)))
> pred_df$lower.CL <- pred_df$emmean - 1.96 * pred_se
> pred_df$upper.CL <- pred_df$emmean + 1.96 * pred_se
> p_model <- ggplot(
>   pred_df,
>   aes(x = Day_nr, y = emmean, color = Group, fill = Group, group = Group)

> day_grid <- 1:10
> pred_df <- expand.grid(
>   Day_nr = day_grid,
>   Group  = levels(dat$Group)
> )
> pred_df <- pred_df %>%
>   mutate(
>     Study_Phase = ifelse(Day_nr <= 5, "Pre-manipulation", "Manipulation"),
>     Study_Phase = factor(Study_Phase, levels = levels(dat$Study_Phase)),
>     Time_Phase = ifelse(Day_nr <= 5, Day_nr - 3, Day_nr - 8),
>     Group = factor(Group, levels = levels(dat$Group))
>   )
> X <- model.matrix(delete.response(terms(m_use)), pred_df)
> V <- vcov(m_use)
> beta <- fixef(m_use)
> pred_df$emmean <- as.numeric(X %*% beta)
> pred_se <- sqrt(diag(X %*% V %*% t(X)))
> pred_df$lower.CL <- pred_df$emmean - 1.96 * pred_se
> pred_df$upper.CL <- pred_df$emmean + 1.96 * pred_se
> p_model <- ggplot(
>   pred_df,
>   aes(x = Day_nr, y = emmean, color = Group, fill = Group, group = Group)
> ) +
>   annotate("rect", xmin = 0.5, xmax = 5.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.08) +
>   annotate("rect", xmin = 5.5, xmax = 10.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.08) +
>   geom_vline(xintercept = 5.5, linetype = "dashed") +
>   annotate("text", x = 3, y = Inf, label = "Pre-manipulation", vjust = 1.2, size = 3.5) +
>   annotate("text", x = 8, y = Inf, label = "Manipulation", vjust = 1.2, size = 3.5) +
>   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), linewidth = 0) +
>   geom_line(linewidth = 2.0) +
>   scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10, limits = c(1, 10)) +
>   scale_y_continuous(
>     limits = c(0, 50),

>   ) +
>   scale_color_manual(values = group_colors_line, breaks = levels(dat$Group), drop = FALSE) +
>   scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors_fill, breaks = levels(dat$Group), drop = FALSE) +

> form_glmm_rs <- as.formula(
>   "Snacking_Healthy_Portions ~ Study_Phase * Group + Time_Phase + Study_Phase:Time_Phase + Study_Phase:Time_Phase:Group + (1 + Study_Phase + Time_Phase || ID)"
> )
> form_glmm_ri <- as.formula(
>   "Snacking_Healthy_Portions ~ Study_Phase * Group + Time_Phase + Study_Phase:Time_Phase + Study_Phase:Time_Phase:Group + (1 | ID)"
> )
> fit_safe <- function(name, fam, zi = FALSE, re = c("rs", "ri")) {
>   re <- match.arg(re)
>   zif <- if (zi) ~ 1 else ~ 0
>   form_use <- if (re == "rs") form_glmm_rs else form_glmm_ri
>   
>   mod <- tryCatch(
>     glmmTMB(form_use, data = dat, family = fam, ziformula = zif),
>     error = function(e) NULL
>   )
>   if (is.null(mod)) return(list(info = NULL, model = NULL))
>   
>   info <- data.frame(
>     Model     = paste0(name, " | RE=", re),
>     Converged = isTRUE(mod$fit$convergence == 0),
>     logLik    = as.numeric(logLik(mod)),
>     df        = attr(logLik(mod), "df"),
>     AIC       = AIC(mod),
>     stringsAsFactors = FALSE
>   )
>   # Keep the resolved family/ZI/random-effect metadata with the fitted model.
>   # This avoids relying on glmmTMB's stored call later (which contains the
>   # local symbol `fam` and therefore cannot safely be re-evaluated by update()).
>   list(info = info, model = mod, family = fam, zi = zi, re = re)
> }
> cand_list_rs <- list(
>   fit_safe("Poisson",                  poisson(), zi = FALSE, re = "rs"),
>   fit_safe("Zero-Infl Poisson (ZIP)", poisson(), zi = TRUE,  re = "rs"),
>   fit_safe("NegBin (nbinom2)",        nbinom2(),  zi = FALSE, re = "rs"),
>   fit_safe("Zero-Infl NegBin (ZINB)", nbinom2(),  zi = TRUE,  re = "rs")
> )
> infos_rs <- lapply(cand_list_rs, `[[`, "info")

> library(lubridate)
> library(glmmTMB)
> library(ggplot2)
> library(tidyr)
> library(emmeans)
> id_col   <- "ID"
> time_col <- "Date_Time"
> base_path <- "../../EMA data/Processed EMA data/"
> dat <- read_xlsx(file.path(base_path, "Merged_Data_All_Conditions.xlsx"))
> stopifnot(all(c(id_col, time_col, "Snacking_Unhealthy_Portions", "Group") %in% names(dat)))
> dat <- dat %>%
>   rename(ID = all_of(id_col), Date_Time = all_of(time_col)) %>%
>   mutate(
>     Date_Time = parse_date_time(
>       as.character(Date_Time),
>       orders = c("Ymd HMS", "Ymd HM", "Ymd", "dmY HMS", "dmY HM", "dmY")
>     ),
>     Group = factor(
>       trimws(as.character(Group)),
>       levels = c("Control_Condition", "Healthy_Condition", "Unhealthy_Condition")
>     ),
>     Snacking_Unhealthy_Portions = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Snacking_Unhealthy_Portions))
>   ) %>%
>   arrange(ID, Date_Time)
> dat <- dat %>%
>   filter(!is.na(Snacking_Unhealthy_Portions)) %>%
>   mutate(
>     Snacking_Unhealthy_Portions = as.integer(round(Snacking_Unhealthy_Portions)),
>     Snacking_Unhealthy_Portions = ifelse(Snacking_Unhealthy_Portions < 0, 0L, Snacking_Unhealthy_Portions)
>   )
> dat <- dat %>%
>   group_by(ID) %>%
>   mutate(
>     Date   = as.Date(Date_Time),
>     Day_nr = match(Date, sort(unique(Date))) # 1,2,3,...
>   ) %>%
>   ungroup()
> dat <- dat %>%
>   mutate(
>     Study_Phase = case_when(
>       Day_nr %in% 1:5  ~ "Pre-manipulation",
>       Day_nr %in% 6:10 ~ "Manipulation",
>       TRUE ~ NA_character_
>     )
>   ) %>%
>   filter(!is.na(Study_Phase), Day_nr %in% 1:10)
> dat$Study_Phase <- factor(dat$Study_Phase, levels = c("Pre-manipulation", "Manipulation"))
> dat <- dat %>%
>   mutate(
>     Time_Phase = case_when(
>       Study_Phase == "Pre-manipulation" ~ Day_nr - 3,
>       Study_Phase == "Manipulation"     ~ Day_nr - 8,
>       TRUE ~ NA_real_
>     )
>   )
> dat <- dat %>%
>   filter(!is.na(ID), !is.na(Group), !is.na(Study_Phase), !is.na(Day_nr), !is.na(Time_Phase))
> vars_to_sum <- c("Snacking_Unhealthy_Portions", "Day_nr")
> summary_overall <- dat %>%

> form_glmm_rs <- as.formula(
>   "Snacking_Unhealthy_Portions ~ Study_Phase * Group + Time_Phase + Study_Phase:Time_Phase + Study_Phase:Time_Phase:Group + (1 + Study_Phase + Time_Phase || ID)"
> )
> form_glmm_ri <- as.formula(
>   "Snacking_Unhealthy_Portions ~ Study_Phase * Group + Time_Phase + Study_Phase:Time_Phase + Study_Phase:Time_Phase:Group + (1 | ID)"
> )
> fit_safe <- function(name, fam, zi = FALSE, re = c("rs", "ri")) {
>   re <- match.arg(re)
>   zif <- if (zi) ~ 1 else ~ 0
>   form_use <- if (re == "rs") form_glmm_rs else form_glmm_ri
>   
>   mod <- tryCatch(
>     glmmTMB(form_use, data = dat, family = fam, ziformula = zif),
>     error = function(e) NULL
>   )
>   if (is.null(mod)) return(list(info = NULL, model = NULL))
>   
>   info <- data.frame(
>     Model     = paste0(name, " | RE=", re),
>     Converged = isTRUE(mod$fit$convergence == 0),
>     logLik    = as.numeric(logLik(mod)),
>     df        = attr(logLik(mod), "df"),
>     AIC       = AIC(mod),
>     stringsAsFactors = FALSE
>   )
>   # Keep the resolved family/ZI/random-effect metadata with the fitted model.
>   # This avoids relying on glmmTMB's stored call later (which contains the
>   # local symbol `fam` and therefore cannot safely be re-evaluated by update()).
>   list(info = info, model = mod, family = fam, zi = zi, re = re)
> }
> cand_list_rs <- list(
>   fit_safe("Poisson",                  poisson(), zi = FALSE, re = "rs"),
>   fit_safe("Zero-Infl Poisson (ZIP)", poisson(), zi = TRUE,  re = "rs"),
>   fit_safe("NegBin (nbinom2)",        nbinom2(),  zi = FALSE, re = "rs"),
>   fit_safe("Zero-Infl NegBin (ZINB)", nbinom2(),  zi = TRUE,  re = "rs")
> )
> infos_rs <- lapply(cand_list_rs, `[[`, "info")
> infos_rs <- Filter(Negate(is.null), infos_rs)
> need_fallback <- TRUE
> if (length(infos_rs) > 0) {
>   aic_rs <- dplyr::bind_rows(infos_rs)
>   if (any(aic_rs$Converged)) need_fallback <- FALSE
> }
> if (need_fallback) {
>   message("NOTE: Phase + Time_Phase random-slope count models failed or did not converge reliably.")
>   message("Refitting candidate models with random intercept only: (1 | ID).")
>   
>   cand_list_ri <- list(
>     fit_safe("Poisson",                  poisson(), zi = FALSE, re = "ri"),
>     fit_safe("Zero-Infl Poisson (ZIP)", poisson(), zi = TRUE,  re = "ri"),
>     fit_safe("NegBin (nbinom2)",        nbinom2(),  zi = FALSE, re = "ri"),
>     fit_safe("Zero-Infl NegBin (ZINB)", nbinom2(),  zi = TRUE,  re = "ri")
>   )
>   
>   cand_list <- cand_list_ri
> } else {
>   cand_list <- cand_list_rs
> }
> infos <- lapply(cand_list, `[[`, "info")
> infos <- Filter(Negate(is.null), infos)
> if (length(infos) == 0) stop("No candidate models could be estimated.")
> aic_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(infos) %>%

> pull_answer <- function(x) {
>   x <- as.character(x)
>   is_json <- !is.na(x) & grepl("answer_content", x, fixed = TRUE)
>   if (any(is_json)) {
>     txt <- sub('.*"answer_content"\\s*:\\s*"([^"]*)".*', "\\1", x[is_json])
>     txt[txt == ""] <- NA_character_
>     x[is_json] <- txt
>   }
>   x
> }
> classify_snack_cat <- function(x) {
>   lx <- tolower(trimws(pull_answer(x)))
>   out <- rep(NA_character_, length(lx))
>   out[lx %in% c("no", "nee")] <- "None"
>   out[grepl("healthy\\s+and\\s+unhealthy", lx)] <- "Both"
>   out[grepl("^yes,?\\s*healthy", lx) &
>         !grepl("healthy\\s+and\\s+unhealthy", lx)] <- "Healthy"
>   out[grepl("^yes,?\\s*unhealthy", lx)] <- "Unhealthy"
>   factor(out, levels = c("None", "Healthy", "Unhealthy", "Both"))
> }
> has_healthy <- function(x) {
>   ifelse(is.na(x), NA_integer_, as.integer(x %in% c("Healthy", "Both")))
> }
> has_unhealthy <- function(x) {
>   ifelse(is.na(x), NA_integer_, as.integer(x %in% c("Unhealthy", "Both")))
> }
> safe_numeric <- function(x, name = deparse(substitute(x))) {
>   x_chr <- as.character(x)
>   out <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x_chr))
>   bad <- !is.na(x_chr) & trimws(x_chr) != "" & is.na(out)
>   if (any(bad)) {
>     cat("  ", name, ": ", sum(bad), " non-numeric value(s) converted to NA\n", sep = "")
>   }
>   out
> }
> pm_decompose <- function(x, id) {
>   person_mean <- ave(
>     x, id,
>     FUN = function(v) if (all(is.na(v))) NA_real_ else mean(v, na.rm = TRUE)
>   )
>   list(within = x - person_mean, between = person_mean)
> }
> fit_glmm_ladder <- function(fixed, data, re_ladder, label = "") {
>   for (re in re_ladder) {
>     form <- as.formula(paste(fixed, "+", re))
>     m <- tryCatch(
>       suppressWarnings(
>         glmer(
>           form,
>           data = data,
>           family = binomial(link = "logit"),
>           control = glmerControl(
>             optimizer = "bobyqa",
>             optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)
>           )
>         )
>       ),
>       error = function(e) NULL
>     )
> 
>     if (!is.null(m)) {
>       conv_msg <- unlist(m@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages)
>       okay <- !isSingular(m, tol = 1e-4) && length(conv_msg) == 0
>       if (okay) {
>         attr(m, "re_used") <- re
>         cat("  [", label, "] random-effects structure: ", re, "\n", sep = "")
>         return(m)
>       }
>     }
>   }
> 
>   # Last resort: fit the simplest candidate and retain it with an explicit warning.
>   re <- tail(re_ladder, 1)
>   form <- as.formula(paste(fixed, "+", re))
>   m <- glmer(
>     form,
>     data = data,
>     family = binomial(link = "logit"),
>     control = glmerControl(
>       optimizer = "bobyqa",
>       optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)
>     )
>   )
>   attr(m, "re_used") <- re
>   cat("  [", label, "] WARNING: retained simplest structure ", re,
>       "; inspect convergence/singularity.\n", sep = "")
>   m
> }
> lrt_focal <- function(m_full, reduced_fixed, data, label = "") {
>   re <- attr(m_full, "re_used")
>   m_red <- glmer(
>     as.formula(paste(reduced_fixed, "+", re)),
>     data = data,
>     family = binomial(link = "logit"),
>     control = glmerControl(
>       optimizer = "bobyqa",
>       optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)
>     )
>   )
>   a <- anova(m_red, m_full, test = "Chisq")

>   tibble(

> phase_followups <- function(model, label) {
>   cat("\n\n--- ", label, ": estimated probabilities ---\n", sep = "")

>   print(em)
> 
>   cat("\nBaseline vs intervention within each condition (link-scale tests):\n")
>   print(summary(pairs(emmeans(model, ~ Phase | Condition)), infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)))
> 
>   cat("\nCondition contrasts within each phase (Tukey adjusted):\n")
>   print(summary(
>     pairs(emmeans(model, ~ Condition | Phase), adjust = "tukey"),
>     infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
>   ))
>   invisible(em)
> }

> pairs_df <- dat %>%
>   arrange(ID, Date, Prompt_nr) %>%
>   group_by(ID, Date) %>%
>   mutate(
>     Prompt1 = lead(Prompt_nr),
>     Phase1 = lead(Phase),
>     SnackCat1 = lead(SnackCat),
>     snack_healthy_t1 = lead(snack_healthy),
>     snack_unhealthy_t1 = lead(snack_unhealthy),
>     IG_use_t1_raw = lead(IG_Use_VAS)
>   ) %>%
>   ungroup() %>%
>   filter(
>     !is.na(Prompt1),
>     Prompt1 == Prompt_nr + 1,
>     !is.na(Phase1),
>     Phase1 == Phase
>   ) %>%
>   mutate(
>     Prompt0_f = factor(Prompt_nr),
>     Prompt0_c = Prompt_nr - mean(Prompt_nr, na.rm = TRUE),
> 
>     # Directional self-regulation requirements and outcomes.
>     sr_required_H = !is.na(intend_healthy) & intend_healthy == 1,
>     sr_required_U = !is.na(intend_unhealthy) & intend_unhealthy == 0,
> 
>     sr_success_H = ifelse(
>       sr_required_H & !is.na(snack_healthy_t1),
>       as.integer(snack_healthy_t1 == 1),
>       NA_integer_
>     ),
>     sr_success_U = ifelse(
>       sr_required_U & !is.na(snack_unhealthy_t1),
>       as.integer(snack_unhealthy_t1 == 0),
>       NA_integer_
>     )
>   )
> cat("\n=== PROSPECTIVE PAIRS ===\n")

> pull_answer <- function(x) {
>   x <- as.character(x)
>   is_json <- !is.na(x) & grepl("answer_content", x, fixed = TRUE)
>   if (any(is_json)) {
>     txt <- sub('.*"answer_content"\\s*:\\s*"([^"]*)".*', "\\1", x[is_json])
>     txt[txt == ""] <- NA_character_
>     x[is_json] <- txt
>   }
>   x
> }
> classify_snack_cat <- function(x) {
>   lx <- tolower(trimws(pull_answer(x)))
>   out <- rep(NA_character_, length(lx))
>   out[lx %in% c("no", "nee")] <- "None"
>   out[grepl("healthy\\s+and\\s+unhealthy", lx)] <- "Both"
>   out[grepl("^yes,?\\s*healthy", lx) &
>         !grepl("healthy\\s+and\\s+unhealthy", lx)] <- "Healthy"
>   out[grepl("^yes,?\\s*unhealthy", lx)] <- "Unhealthy"
>   factor(out, levels = c("None", "Healthy", "Unhealthy", "Both"))
> }
> has_healthy <- function(x) {
>   ifelse(is.na(x), NA_integer_, as.integer(x %in% c("Healthy", "Both")))
> }
> has_unhealthy <- function(x) {
>   ifelse(is.na(x), NA_integer_, as.integer(x %in% c("Unhealthy", "Both")))
> }
> safe_numeric <- function(x, name = deparse(substitute(x))) {
>   x_chr <- as.character(x)
>   out <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x_chr))
>   bad <- !is.na(x_chr) & trimws(x_chr) != "" & is.na(out)
>   if (any(bad)) {
>     cat("  ", name, ": ", sum(bad), " non-numeric value(s) converted to NA\n", sep = "")
>   }
>   out
> }
> pm_decompose <- function(x, id) {
>   person_mean <- ave(
>     x, id,
>     FUN = function(v) if (all(is.na(v))) NA_real_ else mean(v, na.rm = TRUE)
>   )
>   list(within = x - person_mean, between = person_mean)
> }
> fit_brms_model <- function(formula, data, label, priors = priors_default) {
>   cat("\nFitting ", label, " ...\n", sep = "")
>   brm(
>     formula = formula,
>     data = data,
>     family = bernoulli(link = "logit"),
>     prior = priors,
>     chains = N_CHAINS,
>     cores = N_CORES,
>     iter = N_ITER,
>     warmup = N_WARMUP,
>     seed = SEED,
>     control = list(
>       adapt_delta = ADAPT_DELTA,
>       max_treedepth = MAX_TREEDEPTH
>     ),
>     save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
>     refresh = 500
>   )
> }
> fit_with_fallback <- function(form_rs, form_ri, data, label) {
>   m_rs <- fit_brms_model(form_rs, data, paste0(label, " [random slope]"))
> 
>   np <- suppressWarnings(nuts_params(m_rs))
>   n_div <- sum(np$Parameter == "divergent__" & np$Value == 1)
>   summ <- summary(m_rs)
>   max_rhat <- max(summ$fixed[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
> 
>   cat("\nDiagnostics for ", label, ":\n", sep = "")
>   cat("  divergences: ", n_div, "\n", sep = "")
>   cat("  max fixed-effect Rhat: ", round(max_rhat, 4), "\n", sep = "")
> 
>   if (n_div > 0 || is.na(max_rhat) || max_rhat > 1.01) {
>     cat("  Falling back to random-intercept-only model.\n")
>     m_ri <- fit_brms_model(form_ri, data, paste0(label, " [random intercept fallback]"))
>     return(list(model = m_ri, structure = "random intercept"))
>   }
> 
>   list(model = m_rs, structure = "random slope")
> }

Reported vs. reproduced

95 statistical tests reported in the manuscript text were checked against the extracted analysis output: 24 matched (22 fully, 2 partially) — 25.3% found.

Some reported values were only found alongside OTHER components after being separated from their own originally-reported neighbours (e.g. a mean split from its own confidence interval). The “Plausible” column marks whether that split is well-supported: TRUE when the pieces still trace back to the same underlying variable (via the output’s own row labels), FALSE when no such link was found — a FALSE match is not necessarily wrong, but is worth checking against its own Source file/Analysis columns before treating it as confirmed.

SPSS data without syntax

An SPSS data file (.sav/.por) is present but no SPSS syntax file (.sps) was found, so the analysis that produced the results cannot be reproduced from the deposit. This is treated as a reproducibility failure (red). Consider depositing the analysis in jamovi (.omv) or JASP (.jasp) instead: these formats store the data and the analyses together in one file, so the results are reproducible from the file itself.

More detail

Ethics Approval Check

The paper appears to report data that the authors collected from people or animals, and it has an ethics statement.

We based this on:

Method: 116 healthy-weight adults (M age = 22.46 years, 79.3% female) completed a 10-day smartphone ecological momentary assessment protocol (five prompts/day; five baseline, five manipulation days).

Participants were randomly assigned to follow existing preselected Instagram accounts featuring unhealthy food, healthy food, or art (control); the number of additional accounts was 5% of those already followed.

Before the start of the manipulation phase, participants were randomly assigned to follow Instagram accounts featuring unhealthy food, healthy food, or art content.

Ethics statement:

The study was preregistered on AsPredicted (https://aspredicted.org/xb65-zbmb.pdf) and approved by the ethical committee at [university name masked for review] (OZL_250_42_03_2022_S3) and [university name masked for review] (FMG-11882_2024).

Power Analysis Check

We used the LLM model ‘vllm/qwen3-8-27b-fp8’ to check the contents of 1 paragraph that contained words suggesting they might contain power analyses.

All essential information could be detected.

power_type statistical_test sample_size alpha_level power effect_size effect_size_metric software
apriori other 120 0.05 0.9 0.2 Cohen’s d simulation
text
We employed a mixed-design experiment with ten days of EMA measurement. Instagram content condition was included as a between-subjects factor: participants were randomly allocated to either the unhealthy content condition, the healthy content condition, or the control condition. As a withinsubjects …

Cells longer than 300 characters are cut (…).

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen’s d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

Preregistration Check

We found 1 preregistration.

id title template
xb65-zbmb Scroll & Snack: A smartphone EMA study AsPredicted

Meta-scientific research has shown that deviations from preregistrations are often not reported or checked, and that the most common deviations concern the sample size. We recommend manually checking the full preregistration at the link above, and have provided the preregistered sample size.

id sample_size
xb65-zbmb Based on a power analysis simulation using linear mixed effect models, we need 120 participants (40 per BS condition). Power = 90 %, (medium) effect size = 0.2, alpha = .05; CI (99.12 – 100). Sample size was estimated using 50 as number of assessment per participant (ie, 5 prompts/day for 10 days)
